fault_line: The coalition says everything was intercepted; witnesses say the Aramco tower was hit. Who is telling the truth about Riyadh's air defence — a leak, debris, or a cover-up?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Reuters, 4 sources] A tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) was damaged by a projectile on Sunday, one witness and three people briefed on the matter said; Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to requests for comment. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- AFP witnesses, new detail] Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, with shattered glass and parts of the facade visibly affected. [UNCHANGED -- coalition] Saudi air defences intercepted 2 ballistic missiles toward Riyadh + 2 cruise missiles (Riyadh/southern regions) + 1 ballistic toward the Eastern Province on Sunday; at least 15 missiles/UAVs intercepted across the Kingdom in November. [CONTEXT -- Ansar Allah] Saree's Saturday six-operations claim (Riyadh airport, Aramco oil storage/distillation tower, Khurais, Dawadmi Pumping Station No. 8) remains unverified; no Ansar Allah claim for a Sunday KAFD hit has surfaced in-window.
sections.what_verified: 2 independent publisher families (AFP, Reuters), both T1 wires, reporting the same damage with consistent detail from separate witness sets.
sections.what_disputed: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki says all five Sunday missiles were intercepted and destroyed; Saudi Civil Defence later announced the danger had passed; no Saudi or Aramco statement confirms damage; no photo of the damage has been published in-window. Ansar Allah has not claimed a Sunday KAFD hit (its Saturday six-operations claim is a different, unverified claim).
sections.why_matters: LEAD UPDATE -- the financial district was hit: witnesses now number four, and the damage is described floor by floor. The 'all intercepted' story no longer holds on its own. Hard counted number in title: FOUR people / MULTIPLE floors.
